chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us about this, from al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mus'adah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both)
He said: The disbeliever eats with seven intestines

key_terms.الْكَافِرُ: The disbeliever, one who covers or denies the truth
key_terms.سَبْعَةِ أَمْعَاءَ: Seven intestines, indicating a capacity for greater consumption

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that the disbeliever eats with seven intestines?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this concise yet profound statement from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), linking the physical act of eating to spiritual state. While some interpret 'seven intestines' literally as a sign of insatiable worldly appetite, Shia scholars often view it metaphorically, indicating that the disbeliever consumes sustenance without digesting it spiritually, remaining disconnected from divine nourishment. This highlights the contrast between mere physical existence and the refined, purposeful consumption of the faithful.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-29 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Harun ibn Muslim, on the authority of Mus’adat, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), “
The atheists eat with seven intestines. ”
